scope: Reduce rail emphasis; turn schedule into optional reference; navigation independent of lifecycle.
prompt:
Edit the attached HackJudge Code & Tell "Signal rail" homepage concept into a quieter NAVIGATION RAIL revision. Render one high-fidelity wide landscape comparison board with TWO equal desktop homepages: left "Before the session · Zero projects", right "Presentations available · Voting not open". Board title "Code & Tell / Quiet navigation rail"; small "Design concept · Sample event details". Keep the attractive Engineered broad squared title lettering, teal shared identity, white main canvas, cobalt/aqua accent, recognizable asymmetry, all core event title/date/place content and functional buttons. This is a direct evolution of this concept, not a new visual world.

CRITICAL LAYOUT CHANGE: Reduce left rail from about 22% width to only 13–15%, give resulting space to main content. Replace dark NAVY dominating full-height agenda rail with a very light cool gray-blue rail #EFF4F5 against white content, thin understated divider, dark teal text, small normal-width readable sans navigation at 14–16px, compact spacing. Four ordinary anchor navigation items near top: "Overview", "Presentations", "How voting works", "Event details". Selected item has soft pale blue fill and a tiny simple icon or 1px rule, NOT large blue block; the before view selects Overview, presentations view selects Presentations. NO timeline, NO large time numerals, NO connected dots, NO phase progress markings, NO 'now' indicator anywhere in rail. Small event name Code & Tell near rail top optional, no overbearing section title. Quiet rail stays recognizably navigational, not competing with event heading. A small "All events" link can sit low.

Keep MAIN EVENT HEADING visually dominant 'Code & Tell' with Fresh ideas below. November 9, 2026 / Innovation Center. Purpose 'Show what you built. Share what you learned.' The left before view has 'View event' and 'How to participate'. Before view has NO projects, counts, fake presenters or media. Its main region has open comfortable 'Present' and 'Join in' guidance with concise readable copy, lightly tinted aqua region at most, much quieter than original giant colored cards. Remove invented '5 minutes per presentation'. Lower main content has concise audience ballot explanation and a small 'Event details' disclosure row.

Right view MAIN CONTENT has plain section 'Presentations', two rows 'Voltify / Community energy-demand forecasting' and 'AgriSense / Field sensors and crop insights'. The numeric 01/02 may be removed or made small and quiet; do not imply rankings. No time-based 'Session underway', 'Happening now' or active demo status. A current voting status is safe only labeled as source-confirmed: a compact clear 'Voting not yet open' info region and copy 'You can cast your ballot when the organizer opens voting.' This is an illustrative actual permission state, not a clock prediction. Main action remains View event, no vote action yet.

PLANNED AGENDA: all four original agenda times must disappear from navigation and from voting status copy. Show only a quiet collapsed row in Event details labeled 'Planned schedule' with a disclosure chevron and small supporting note 'Times may change. Follow organizer announcements.' No auto-advance, countdown, active time highlighting, or 'Voting opens at 18:00' text ANYWHERE. If any session-underway label is shown it must explicitly read 'Organizer update: Presentations underway', but prefer omit entirely for clean composition.

Bottom secondary 'Coming up' calendar sample CivicHacks Dec 5 and Community showcase Dec 12, All events link remains secondary. No hackathon challenge tracks, no expert scoring rubrics, no appreciation hearts. Readable actual UI, not poster, no new illustration, no gradients, no glow, no physical device frame. Colors and typography preserve the selected Engineered identity. The design must clearly show that event identity, participation and projects command attention; navigation quietly supports them and schedule is optional reference.
